title: Giant umbrella-cap mushroom
description: An oversized shallow mushroom cap sits on a long, narrow stalk among the grotto rocks.
adaptation: Proposal: use its clear cap-and-stalk silhouette as a large cover landmark beside an open dash floor.
notes: The still establishes appearance and scale, not the growth animation or a biological species.

title: Low mushroom cluster
description: Several low, rounded mushroom caps appear at different sizes near the foreground and rock shelves.
adaptation: Proposal: group a small shared set of caps into readable edge dressing or low blockers.
notes: Keep this clustered form distinct from the tall landmark mushroom; the film does not establish a pickup function.

title: Porous grotto foreground forms
description: Rounded foreground forms have a conspicuous dark cellular or honeycomb pattern.
adaptation: Proposal: reuse the porous pattern on a few fungal scenery pieces along the arena edges.
notes: The entry names the visible pattern rather than asserting an exact fungus or coral species.

title: Fallen trunk crossing
description: A long, irregular trunk-like form stretches horizontally across the grotto foreground.
adaptation: Proposal: use the trunk as a threshold or broad crossing motif with enough landing space for the normal dash.
notes: Its game collision width is a design proposal; do not derive a narrow precision platform from the film image.

title: Pointed grotto ceiling
description: An irregular overhanging rock silhouette with downward points frames the upper part of the cave.
adaptation: Proposal: build shared upper and side scenery flats from this silhouette and keep them clear of combat warnings.
notes: Visual reference only; this entry does not establish the original set's construction materials.

title: Grotto rock shelves
description: Uneven horizontal rock shelves step into the grotto background between the mushrooms.
adaptation: Proposal: layer shelf sprites behind a flat playable floor to suggest depth without adding mandatory precision climbing.
notes: Distinct from the exposed lunar crater floor: these shelves belong to the enclosed grotto composition.

title: Rib-banded Selenite costume
description: The standing Selenites have humanoid bodies with repeated pale bands across their dark torsos.
adaptation: Proposal: retain the biped body and pale rib pattern in the enemy sprite instead of using a crawling beetle body.
notes: The film frame supports the visible costume pattern. The 1960 Labisse reconstruction is separate evidence and does not establish 1902 materials.

title: Selenite projecting headpiece
description: Selenite heads have conspicuous projecting points or antenna-like elements above the humanoid costume.
adaptation: Proposal: use two or three large head projections as a readable pixel silhouette for the enemy family.
notes: Exact mask details are limited by the still resolution; consult the film before producing a faithful costume reconstruction.

title: Oversized arrowhead spear
description: Several long upright shafts end in bright, oversized triangular spearheads.
adaptation: Proposal: preserve the exaggerated arrowhead to make a guard's close-range attack direction visible during its windup.
notes: Enemy attack timing and reach are game proposals, not inferred from the still.

title: Seated Selenite royal figure
description: A conspicuous costumed figure sits in the royal area at the left of the court tableau, with an exaggerated head silhouette.
adaptation: Proposal: use the theatrical seated figure as the reference for the earlier Selenite King boss.
notes: The game's King encounter is an adaptation; the still does not define a boss combat pattern.

title: Low royal seat and base
description: The royal figure is seated above a low decorated base at the left side of the court tableau.
adaptation: Proposal: place a compact throne landmark at the edge of a broad court arena, leaving the dash floor open.
notes: The frame gives the silhouette and placement; exact joinery, dimensions, and materials are unverified.

title: Radiant circular court roundel
description: A large circular ornament with long radial rays and a star-like centre stands behind the royal side of the tableau.
adaptation: Proposal: use the radial roundel as a bold court backdrop motif and reuse smaller versions on optional-room scenery.
notes: Described as a visual ornament; this entry does not assign an astronomical or religious identity to it.

title: Crescent-topped court column
description: A tall decorated vertical support is crowned by a large crescent silhouette.
adaptation: Proposal: use a shared crescent-column asset to mark court boundaries and entrances.
notes: The crescent is an observed motif; making the column destructible or interactive would be a separate proposal.

title: Curtained ornamental court arch
description: A large rounded ornamental opening at the right of the court contains gathered dark drapery.
adaptation: Proposal: reuse the arch and curtain as the doorway frame for regular and optional court rooms.
notes: The image supports drapery and the rounded frame; do not turn it into Gothic pointed masonry by default.

title: Curling court ornament panels
description: The court backdrop contains dense curving, curling, and repeated ornamental lines.
adaptation: Proposal: build a small set of painted ornamental panels that can be rearranged around multiple arenas.
notes: Use broad readable curves at game scale; tiny ornament need not be reproduced literally.

title: Dense white disappearance puff
description: A bright dense cloud occupies the centre of the lunar exterior frame and obscures the area behind it.
adaptation: Proposal: interpret the white puff as square smoke particles that accompany an enemy defeat while keeping the floor readable.
notes: The still verifies the puff's visible appearance, not animation timing, duration, cause, or the exact instant of disappearance.

title: Projecting escape ledge
description: An irregular rock lip projects over an open void beneath the angled capsule.
adaptation: Proposal: use the overhang silhouette at an exit or cinematic boundary, with a generous playable approach.
notes: A fatal drop or dash puzzle is not established by the frame and must be designed separately.

title: Hanging escape cord
description: A thin cord-like line hangs downward below the capsule and rock edge.
adaptation: Proposal: add the cord to an escape vignette built from the existing capsule and rock assets.
notes: The still alone does not verify a rope-pulling sequence or physics behaviour.

title: Capsule-clinging Selenite pose
description: A humanoid Selenite is positioned against the capsule exterior with its arms raised toward the shell.
adaptation: Proposal: create a hitchhiker pose or brief animation by reusing the Selenite character and capsule assets.
notes: This is a distinct scene pose, not a new enemy species or a replacement capsule design.

title: Tall-masted harbour ship
description: A ship silhouette in the harbour has tall masts and many thin rigging lines above a dark hull.
adaptation: Proposal: use a layered ship-and-rigging backdrop for a short Earth-return vignette.
notes: The entry records its visible silhouette rather than a precise vessel class or scale.

title: Low harbour rescue vessel
description: A low vessel-like silhouette crosses the harbour, with a semicircular wheel-like shape visible along its side.
adaptation: Proposal: use the low silhouette as the rescue vessel in a return scene without building a new playable transport system.
notes: The small still does not resolve engineering details; the rescue role is an adaptation of the return sequence.

title: Foreground harbour quay
description: A dark quay or pier edge projects into the foreground at the right, beside the ship and water.
adaptation: Proposal: reuse its projecting edge as a hub border or return-scene foreground layer.
notes: Surface materials and structural details are not established by this image.

title: Towering water-splash plume
description: A tall, very bright plume rises from the harbour water and dominates the left side of the frame.
adaptation: Proposal: translate the plume into a brief square-particle splash during the Earth-return transition.
notes: The still verifies the visible plume, not animation timing, duration, force, or particle trajectories.

title: Astronomer commemorative monument
description: A monument shows an astronomer with a raised hand and umbrella, with one foot above a Moon-face bearing the capsule in its eye.
adaptation: Proposal: use this exaggerated monument as an epilogue landmark or replay-menu backdrop.
notes: The game may reinterpret its narrative meaning; it is not a reference for the Man in the Moon's combat behaviour.

title: Wreathed monument plinth
description: The monument stands on a rectangular decorated plinth with a wreath on its front and an inscription band near the top.
adaptation: Proposal: reuse the plinth shape as a civic marker while keeping text and ornament legible at pixel scale.
notes: No exact inscription transcription is asserted here.

title: Painted period-town frontage
description: Period building fronts with small windows, rooflines, and turret-like forms fill the background behind the monument and crowd.
adaptation: Proposal: build a compact shared Earth-town backdrop that can also appear beyond the observatory and launch area.
notes: The architecture is recorded as a painted-looking visual composition, not assigned to a specific real city.

title: Hat-raising celebration crowd
description: Celebrants behind the front line hold several hats aloft around the commemorative monument.
adaptation: Proposal: reuse the astronomer and period-citizen sprites in a few cheering poses for the chapter epilogue.
notes: The still verifies the lifted hats and crowd arrangement, not the timing of a cheering animation. The sailor front line reuses the earlier attendant costume and is not counted as a new object here.

title: Horizontal harbour reflection streaks
description: Bright horizontal streaks and dark bands depict reflections across the foreground harbour water.
adaptation: Proposal: use a restrained looping pixel water texture or static painted bands beneath the return-scene vessels.
notes: A still does not establish how the water was animated or how the original effect was constructed.
